newsitem.title: UK: Wet Brent trades lower, March barrels still ample.
newsitem.headline: Wet Brent trades lower, March barrels still ample.

text.p: - North Sea wet Brent traded over 20 cents weaker on Wednesday with March barrels still plentiful and the April loading programme looming.
A March 25-27 cargo traded at April Brent -50 cents, while a March 22-24 cargo fetched just April -60 cents, compared to Tuesday's traded levels of April -37 cents.
"There's still plenty more March (barrels) to go and no much time to sell it," said one trader.
Nevertheless some thought that wet Brent had reached its floor at new lower levels. "I'd say (April minus) 50 to 60 is pretty fair value," one said.

The sole Brent cargo nominated from the paper chains on Wednesday, due to load March 27-29, was kept by BP ahead of the five o'clock deadline. Another cargo is due to come through the chains on Thursday, while the final three March Brents will turn wet on Friday.

Other North Sea grades also looked weaker as sellers rushed to dispose of March barrels. An Oseberg loading March 24-26 fetched just Dated Brent minus one cent, and a Statfjord was rumoured to have also traded at a discount to Dated.
Bucking the trend was Ekofisk, which traded at a firmer Dated Brent +14 cents for a March 25-27 loader.

A Russian sour Urals cargo was bought by a Scandinavian refiner at Dated Brent -90 cents cif Rotterdam, while Urals values in the Mediterranean slipped to around at Dated Brent -$1.20 basis Augusta, having traded at Dated -$1.30 into Israel.
On paper, the April/May Brent intermonth spread eased back having been bid up aggressively by a Wall Street trader.
April/May traded several times at a high of +22 cents, having fetched just +6 cents earlier. The spread softened to talk at +15/20 cents in late trade, while May/June traded at +5 cents.
"(The trading house) just moved in and bought everything it could in half an hour.
